result.topic_en: Dated entries from late 1796 to January 1797 in Gauss's mathematical diary, covering roots of x^p-1=0, multipliers of equations, interpolation, series in powers of ω, trigonometric series, generalized differentiation, parabolic quadrature, Lagrange's theorem and integrals reduced by the substitution yy = sin x or cos x.

items.english: The roots of the equation x^p-1=0, multiplied by integers and added together, cannot produce zero.

items.quote:
Quaedam sese obtulerunt de multiplicatoribus
aequationum ut certi termini eiiciantur, quae
praeclara pollicentur
items.english: Some things have presented themselves concerning multipliers of equations, so that certain terms are eliminated, which promise excellent results.

items.quote:
Lex detecta: quando et demonstrata erit
systema ad perfectionem evexerimus
items.english: Law discovered: when it has also been proved, we will have brought the system to perfection.

items.quote:
Incepi expressionem $1-\frac{1}{2^\omega}+\frac{1}{3^\omega}\ldots$ in seriem
transmutare secundum potestates ipsius
$\omega$ progredientem.
items.english: I began to transform the expression 1 - 1/2^ω + 1/3^ω ... into a series progressing in powers of ω.

items.quote:
Curvam parabolicam quadrare suscepi.
cuius puncta quotcunque dantur
items.english: I undertook to find the area under a parabolic curve of which any number of points are given.
I discovered a genuine proof of Lagrange's theorem.
